Lead notes.
- Target weight is not set, I do not have your current or goal weight. Tell me your current and target weight so final cut guidance can be added.
- Primary goal is speed and it is being preserved in the late-camp sharpness touches shown on D-5 and the alactic work across SPP. Balance is a limiter so there are single-leg, landing, and stability touches each week to keep that limiter exposed without adding heavy volume.

GPP — Week 1 (D-52 to D-46) — Restore structural tolerance and start low-damage repeatability

D-52 (Wednesday) — Strength
Why: build repeated power and upper-body control without heavy soreness.
- Kettlebell Swing: 3 sets x 5 reps; rest 90 sec.
  Cue: Hinge at the hips, drive with your hips and let the bell float to chest level.
  Purpose: develop repeated hip drive for punch speed and torque.
  Progress: next session try 4 sets x 5 reps.
  Easier: use a lighter kettlebell and keep crisp speed.
  Stop: Stop the set when your snap speed slows or you cannot keep posture.
- Single-Leg Forward Hops: 3 sets x 4 reps per leg; rest 90 sec.
  Cue: land softly and balance before the next hop, hold the landing 1 sec.
  Purpose: train single-leg power and landing balance.
  Progress: next session add 2 reps per set (3 x 6/leg).
  Easier: step-hops instead of full jumps.
  Stop: Stop the set if landing control is lost.
- DB Alternating Incline Press (30-45°): 2 sets x 8 reps; rest 90 sec; RPE 6.
  Cue: press explosively on the way up, control the way down.
  Purpose: keep shoulder strength and quick pressing for guard control.
  Progress: next session add 1 set.
  Easier: reduce load or do single-arm seated press.
  Stop: Stop if shoulder pain increases.
- Battle Rope Slams: 2 sets x 8 reps; rest 90 sec; RPE 6.
  Cue: use hips and core, keep arms relaxed, full reset between reps.
  Purpose: add short repeated upper-body power without heavy load.
  Progress: next session add 1 set.
  Easier: slow the tempo and reduce rope amplitude.
  Stop: Stop if lower back or shoulder technique breaks.

D-52 (Wednesday) — Low aerobic gas-tank support
Why: keep the aerobic base without creating fatigue.
- Easy Assault Bike: 25 min continuous; nasal breathing only; RPE 3-4.
  Cue: keep cadence steady, breathe through the nose, keep posture tall.
  Purpose: rebuild aerobic repeatability and speed recovery between efforts.
  Progress: next session add 5 min.
  Easier: drop to 15-20 min at the same effort.
  Stop: Stop if breathing becomes forced or you feel dizzy.

D-52 (Wednesday) — Ring Cut-Off Walkdown
Why: Control space and cut the ring by closing angles, not chasing. Low mechanical cost; a taper-safe pressure pattern.
- Ring Cut-Off Walkdown: 2 x 90 sec technical sets, 60 sec reset
  Cue: Follow a self-planned or random visual escape path and close the angle without crossing the feet or chasing.
  Cue Method: Self-administer a random visual cue (reaction-cue app or a randomized left/right/shot call sequence) so the read stays genuinely reactive without a helper.
  Side / Stance: Work both directions evenly from your normal stance.

D-47 (Monday) — Aerobic support
Why: add low-noise aerobic minutes to keep the gas tank ticking.
- Easy Assault Bike: 25 min continuous; nasal breathing only; RPE 3-4.
  Cue: breathe through the nose, smooth pedal stroke.
  Purpose: steady aerobic base and recovery between harder sessions.
  Progress: next session add 5 min.
  Easier: reduce time to 20 min.
  Stop: Stop if breathing becomes forced or you feel dizzy.

D-40 (Monday) — Strength
Why: keep lower-body power and single-leg balance under controlled load.
- Kettlebell Swing: 3 sets x 5 reps; rest 90 sec.
  Cue: hinge hard and snap hips, keep chest tall.
  Purpose: repeated hip drive for punch speed and power.
  Progress: next session try 4 sets x 5 reps.
  Easier: reduce weight and keep crisp speed.
  Stop: Stop if snap speed drops or form breaks.
- Single-Leg Forward Hops: 3 sets x 4 reps per leg; rest 90 sec.
  Cue: land softly and hold the landing briefly.
  Purpose: challenge single-leg power and balance.
  Progress: next session add 2 reps per set.
  Easier: do step-hops for control.
  Stop: Stop if landing control is lost.
- DB Alternating Incline Press (30-45°): 2 sets x 8 reps; rest 90 sec; RPE 6.
  Cue: press with intent, lower with control.
  Purpose: keep shoulder and pressing quick for guard and push-offs.
  Progress: next session add 1 set.
  Easier: reduce weight.
  Stop: Stop if shoulder pain worsens.

D-33 (Monday) — Strength
Why: start pairing heavy control and explosive transfer for fighting power.
- Jump Lunge (Alternating): 4 sets x 3 reps total (alternating; 3 reps = 3 landings per leg pair); rest 90 sec.
  Cue: explode up, land softly, reset stance each rep.
  Purpose: train quick alternating leg drive and landing control.
  Progress: next session add 1 rep per set.
  Easier: do walking lunges at tempo.
  Stop: Stop if knee tracking or landing control breaks.
- Heavy RDL → Broad Jump: 3 rounds. Heavy movement 2 reps @ controlled heavy load; rest 30-60 sec then Broad Jump 2 reps at max intent; rest 3 min between rounds.
  Cue: control the heavy pull, then explode into broad jumps with full reset.
  Purpose: pair strength with explosive horizontal power.
  Progress: next session add one round.
  Easier: reduce heavy load or do Romanian deadlift to mid-shin.
  Stop: Stop if low back pain increases.
- Sled Push (Speed): 3 carries x 20 m; full rest between carries.
  Cue: drive with legs and keep posture high.
  Purpose: develop horizontal force and drive without impact.
  Progress: next session add one carry.
  Easier: push lighter load or shorter distance.
  Stop: Stop if posture collapses.

D-29 (Friday) — Aerobic support

D-19 (Monday) — Strength
Why: keep ballistic power and speed under specific loads.
- Barbell Thruster: 4 sets x 3 reps at max speed; full rest 90-120 sec.
  Cue: drop under the bar and drive with legs, finish with an explosive press.
  Purpose: full-body ballistic power for rotational and vertical transfer.
  Progress: next session add 1 rep if technique is perfect.
  Easier: reduce load and focus on speed only.
  Stop: Stop if technique breaks or shoulder pain appears.
- Lateral Bound-to-Slip: 4 sets x 3 reps each side; rest 90-120 sec.
  Cue: explode laterally, land softly and slip the head off the centerline.
  Purpose: lateral quickness and defensive slip transfer.
  Progress: next session add 1 rep.
  Easier: do single lateral hops without slip.
  Stop: Stop if landing control breaks.
- Landmine Push Press: 2 sets x 8 reps; rest 120 sec; RPE 6-7.
  Cue: use a split stance, drive through the floor, finish fast.
  Purpose: shoulder and trunk drive that matches punching angles.
  Progress: next session add 1 set.
  Easier: reduce range of motion or weight.
  Stop: Stop if shoulder pain increases.

SPP — Week 6 (D-18 to D-13) — Peak specificity, protect freshness

D-17 (Wednesday) — Shadowboxing Aerobic Flow
Why: keep the gas tank ticking with very low cost movement.
- 4 x 2 min easy solo movement rounds, 60 sec rest.
  Cue: smooth sport-specific movement at RPE 3, no power or impact.
  Purpose: maintain movement and breathing without costing freshness.

D-16 (Thursday) — Aerobic support
Why: keep fight-pace footwork density with controlled cost.
- Pressure Footwork Flow: 3 rounds x 180 sec work; rest 45 sec.
  Cue: stalk at a controlled pace, reset stance after each entry.
  Purpose: preserve footwork repeatability under low-moderate load.
  Progress: next session add 1 round.
  Easier: shorten rounds.
  Stop: Stop if you start chasing or crossing feet.

D-16 (Thursday) — Alactic sharpness
Why: keep short explosive entries for speed quality.
- Entry-Score-Exit Bursts: 8 x 6 sec work; rest 60 sec; RPE 8.
  Cue: explosive step-in, land 1-3 clean shots, exit at an angle and reset.
  Purpose: train quick entries, scoring, and exit under speed demands.
  Progress: none this block, hold dose and quality.
  Easier: reduce rounds to 4.
  Stop: Stop if speed and form fall apart.
- Straight-Shot Re-Angle: 8 x 6 sec work; rest 60 sec; RPE 8.
  Cue: fire a fast straight, retract, and make a 30-45 degree exit.
  Purpose: practice straight-line scoring and re-angle for follow-up.
  Progress: none this block, hold dose and quality.
  Easier: reduce rounds to 4.
  Stop: Stop if technique degrades.

TAPER — Week 7 (D-12 to D-6) — Strip out fatigue and keep sharpness

D-12 (Monday) — Neural speed touch
Why: short neural primer to keep first-step speed.
- Explosive Straight Burst: 2 x 5 sec; rest 120 sec.
  Cue: tiny explosive first step and retract immediately.
  Purpose: preserve first-step speed without building fatigue.
  Progress: none this block, keep dose and do not increase.
  Easier: reduce to 1 x 5 sec.
  Stop: Stop if you feel any sharp pain or major fatigue.
- Pocket Frame-Burst Touch: 1 x 5 sec; rest 120 sec.
  Cue: press into pocket frame and out, crisp and brief.
  Purpose: maintain pocket burst and recovery timing.
  Progress: none this block.
  Easier: do a slow rehearsal instead.
  Stop: Stop if you lose stability.
- Pull-Counter-Reset: 1 x 5 sec; rest 120 sec.
  Cue: pull a small counter and reset position, stay crisp.
  Purpose: keep pull-counter timing and reset mechanics.
  Progress: none this block.
  Easier: perform as a pause and reset drill.
  Stop: Stop if technique collapses.

TAPER — Week 8 (D-5 to D-0) — Fight-week survival and rhythm

D-5 (Monday) — Freshness primer
Why: final short speed cue to preserve sharpness.
- Explosive First-Step Cue: 2 x 5 sec; rest 120 sec.
  Cue: tiny, full-intent first-step, land ready to defend.
  Purpose: keep first-step snap without causing fatigue.
  Progress: none this block.
  Easier: reduce to 1 x 5 sec.
  Stop: Stop immediately if you feel any soreness.
- Pocket Frame-Burst Touch: 1 x 5 sec; rest 120 sec.
  Cue: brief pressure into the pocket then reset.
  Purpose: keep pocket timing and quickness.
  Progress: none this block.
  Easier: do a slow rehearsal.
  Stop: Stop if stability is lost.
- Pull-Counter-Reset: 1 x 5 sec; rest 120 sec.
  Cue: small counter pull then settle.
  Purpose: keep the counter habit sharp.
  Progress: none this block.
  Easier: skip if you feel flat.
  Stop: Stop if you feel unwell.

Notes and rules summary.
- No extra S&C is added to declared hard-sparring/contact days. Those days are your gym-run combat days.
- If you want the plan to include a weight-cut protocol, tell me both your current weight and your target weight and I will add a short, stage-appropriate cut plan.
- If any session feels sharper than planned, reduce volume first and keep the technical primers unchanged.

End of plan.
